title: Horizon update guides rhythm planning
query: A horizon lane run has fresh external context, memory reports, skill hardening reports, and ticket outcomes. What should it produce?
reference_points: Synthesizes strategy rather than executing leaf tickets
Uses report freshness and labels missing/stale inputs
Checks drift against original goals, mission, and the current milestone
Produces n-week priorities and constraints for rhythm-update
Converts actionable changes into ticket deltas or Goal Advisor handoffs
Writes horizon report and ledger freshness

title: Horizon update is not a status digest
query: The horizon update has many reports but no obvious metric improvements. What should it avoid, and what should it do instead?
reference_points: Avoids summarizing reports without decisions
Names kept, changed, paused, killed, or testable bets
Labels missing feedback or metrics instead of inventing KPIs
Creates ticket deltas or feedback/instrumentation gaps when needed
Keeps pulse or rhythm noise from dominating horizon strategy

title: Horizon update accepts context refs instead of hard-coded sources
query: A project wants horizon planning using goals.md, tickets/, metrics.jsonl, meeting-notes.md, and a Codex thread index. How should horizon-update receive and use these inputs?
reference_points: Accepts context refs or files as params
Writes a bounded context bundle before synthesis or lane delegation
Labels missing refs as source gaps
Does not hard-code Kenji's Notion or life paths in the generic skill
May route to weekly-strategy-analysis as a specialized wrapper when personal refs are supplied

title: Horizon update separates reports from goals promotion
query: A horizon run finds evidence that a KPI may be wrong and that a current_signal reference is stale. What should it do before editing goals.md?
reference_points: Writes the context bundle and horizon report before mutating goals.md
Puts both changes in a Goals Delta block with evidence
Auto-applies only the low-risk stale current_signal or source-ref update when evidence is clear
Marks KPI changes as approval_required instead of silently patching them
Creates a source gap or instrumentation ticket when evidence is insufficient

title: Horizon update treats quarterly and yearly work as scheduled actions
query: A project asks the horizon lane to add quarterly and yearly KPI schedules because those horizons may matter later. What is the default behavior?
reference_points: Treats quarterly and yearly planning as due scheduled actions inside horizon-update by default
Does not create a new persistent lane or thread without evidence that it adds value
Uses horizon reports as the rolling context source for longer-horizon reviews
Requires approval for quarterly or yearly goal/KPI portfolio changes
Records the decision and evidence in the horizon report
